title: How Many Words Should a Product Description Be?
summary: There's no fixed word count for a product description. Length depends on what the shopper needs to know. See length by product type, channel limits and the SEO answer.
body_markdown:
There's no fixed number of words a product description should be. A familiar, low-cost item can be covered in a few sentences, while a technical or expensive one needs more room for specs and the questions shoppers ask before they buy. The right length is the shortest one that answers those questions.


Channels add their own rules on top. Walmart asks for at least 150 words, and Google Shopping shows only the start of a description.


## How long should a product description be?


Long enough to answer what a shopper needs to know before buying, and no longer. That depends more on the product than on any word target. A shopper buying a phone charger needs to know it fits their phone and how fast it charges. A shopper buying a sofa wants dimensions, materials, comfort, care and delivery details.


Product type What the shopper needs to know Typical length


Everyday, familiar items (basic apparel, consumables) Size or material, and the one detail that sets it apart A few sentences


Mid-price items with options (shoes, small appliances) Fit or dimensions, materials, care, how it compares to similar items A short paragraph plus bullets


Technical, expensive or new-to-the-shopper items (electronics, furniture) Specs, compatibility, use cases, setup and care A paragraph plus bullets and a spec table


These are a starting point. If shoppers keep asking customer service the same question, the answer belongs in the description.


### Bullets or paragraphs


Most product pages work best with both. A short paragraph explains what the product is and who it's for. Bullets carry the facts shoppers scan for, such as dimensions and what's in the box. Specs that are pure data, like voltage or weight, read best in a table.


Channels decide part of this for you. Walmart wants the description as one paragraph with no bullets and the features in a separate key features field. Amazon puts bullet points above the description, so the bullets do most of the work there.


### Set the length by category, not by product


On a catalog with thousands of SKUs, decide the length and structure once for each category, such as how many bullets to use and which specs to include. For example, every phone case can follow one template, with the same specs in the same order. This keeps descriptions consistent across the category and gives writers, or an AI writer, a clear brief.

## How long should a product description be for SEO?


There's no minimum word count for ranking.[Google's own guidance on helpful content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/creating-helpful-content) lists writing to a particular word count as a warning sign and says it doesn't have a preferred word count.


What helps a product page rank is a description that's unique to the product and answers what shoppers search for. That means the product's key attributes and the terms people use to describe it. A short description written for one product may do more than a long template repeated across a category, which creates the[duplicate product descriptions](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/duplicate-product-descriptions-seo) problem.


Length starts to matter when a page is too thin to show what the product is. A description that's only the product name and a color gives search engines and AI shopping assistants nothing to match a shopper's question to.


## What are the product description limits on Amazon, Walmart and Google Shopping?


Each channel sets its own limits, and they change, so check the current rules before you write to them. As of November 2026:


Channel Title Bullets or key features Description


[Amazon](https://sellercentral.amazon.com/help/hub/reference/external/G200390640) Up to 75 characters, including spaces, for all product types except media At least three bullet points; character limits vary by product type Limits set per product type in each listing template


[Walmart Marketplace](https://marketplacelearn.walmart.com/guides/Item%20setup/Item%20content,%20imagery,%20and%20media/Product-Detail-Page:-overview) Up to 150 characters 3 to 10 key features, up to 80 characters each One paragraph of at least 150 words, with requirements that vary by category; no bullet points


[Google Merchant Center](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324468) Set by the title attribute Not applicable Up to 5,000 characters, with the most important details in the first 160 to 500 characters


The limits differ enough that one description rarely fits every channel. A description with bullets written for your own site needs reworking into one paragraph for Walmart and front-loaded facts for Google Shopping, where shoppers see only the opening before they click.


## Frequently asked questions


### Can I use AI to write product descriptions?


Yes. AI can write descriptions from your product data in bulk, which helps most on large catalogs where writing each one by hand isn't practical.[Automated product descriptions](https://www.hypotenuse.ai/blog/ai-automated-product-descriptions) are only as good as the data they start from, so fill missing attributes first and review a sample from each category before publishing.


### How many words should a short description be?


Where your platform has a separate short description field, keep it to one or two sentences. It often shows next to the price or in search results, so lead with what the product is and its main benefit.


### What should a product description include?


What the product is and who it's for, plus the facts a shopper checks before buying, such as size or dimensions, materials, compatibility and what's in the box. Use the words shoppers search with, and answer the questions customer service hears most about that product.
